BURHAN:v2p129/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p129/r3.claim: The hadith that actions depend on intentions has an explicit Quranic basis in the contrast between seeking the immediate world and the Hereafter, and in accountability for what hearts intend and oaths they bind.
BURHAN:v2p129/r3.anchor: ثم بدأ رضى الله عنه بحديث ( إنما الأعمال بالنيات ) وقال موضعه نصافي قوله تعالى

DAMGHANI:v1p237/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r1.claim: Saʿy means work or action; the examples describe a person’s effort and work being accepted.
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r1.anchor: يقول وعمل لها عملها وقوله تعالى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Section III invites Jews and Quraysh to the Qur’an's natural straight path, contrasts the fates of acceptance and rejection, rebukes those blind to signs who demand punishment, and alludes to God's practice of punishing nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: both the Jews and the Idolaters of the Quraysh are invited to profess faith in the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Those who seek the Hereafter and make the fitting effort succeed there while receiving whatever worldly share God ordained for them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: these people who earn in this world whatever is ordained for them and the hereafter is already an abode of success for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Desire for the Hereafter alone is insufficient: it must be joined to fitting effort and faith free of polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they also require a befitting effort and a faith too that is devoid of any stain of polytheism.

BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r1.claim: Seeking the afterlife requires its fitting effort: obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions, not invented devotional practices; the lām marks intention and sincerity.
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r1.anchor: السعي اللائق بها وهو الإتيان بما أمر والانتهاء عما نهى لا التقرب بما يخترعون بآرائهم

BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r2.claim: The seeker must also have sound faith without association or denial; these three conditions yield effort accepted by God and rewarded, with gratitude meaning reward for obedience.
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r2.anchor: الجامعون الشرائط الثلاثة من إرادة الآخرة والسعي الجميل لها والإيمان

BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r3.claim: Human beings combine worldly and otherworldly elements: the lower self tends toward Hell, the spirit toward Paradise, and the heart can turn toward either divine wrath or grace.
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r3.anchor: خلق الإنسان مركبا من الدنيا والآخرة ولكل جزء منهما ميل وإرادة إلى كله

BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r4.claim: By divine wrath a heart turns toward worldly desire and separation; by grace it turns upward, seeks the afterlife sincerely, and trusts that whoever seeks God finds Him, so its effort is appreciated by the eternal Originator.
BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r4.anchor: ومن يرد الله به أن يكون مظهر لطفه أقام قلبه وحول وجهه إلى عالم العلو

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r1.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking its lasting abode and blessings, while its proper effort is fulfilling commands and avoiding prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر على طبق ما مر عن الضحاك أن يراد بعمله أيضا ( الآخرة ( أي الدار الآخرة وما فيها من النعيم المقيم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r2.claim: Some construe the effort as an act done for the afterlife or as effort suited to it; either way, invented worship by unbelievers does not qualify.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r2.anchor: وسعى لها سعيها ( أي الذي يحق ويليق بها كما تنبيء عنه الإضافة الاختصاصية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r3.claim: The lām signals purpose or special relation and thus requires intention and sincerity toward God in the deed.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r3.anchor: وفائدة اللام سواء كانت للأجل أو للاختصاص اعتبار النية والإخلاص لله تعالى في العمل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r4.claim: Some say there is no need to understand the earlier desire as desire through deeds, since the following phrase already describes the effort; on this reading the same need not be supplied for the prior verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r4.anchor: واختار بعضهم ولا يخلو عن حسن أنه لا حاجة إلى ما اعتبره الضحاك بل الأولى عدم اعتباره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r5.claim: The person must have sound faith, and the circumstantial clause shows faith must accompany both desire and effort; without it neither suffices.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r5.anchor: إيمانا صحيحا لا يخالطه قادح وإيراد الإيمان بالجملة الحالية للدلالة على اشتراط مقارنته لما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r6.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r6.claim: A saying from an early authority says useful work requires firm faith, sincere intention, and sound action, and cites this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r6.anchor: عن بعض المتقدمين من لم يكن معه ثلاث لم ينفعه عمله إيمان ثابت ونية صادقة وعمل مصيب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r7.claim: Those points to the people just described; the plural both respects the meaning of من and hints that their reward arrives together, while their elevated status is signaled by distance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r7.anchor: وما في ذلك من معنى البعد للإشعار بعلو درجتهم وبعد منزلتهم والجمعية لمراعاة جانب المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r8.claim: Their effort is accepted and rewarded; commentators differ on whether سعي refers to all the prior qualifying deeds or only the effort just named, whose centrality the wording highlights.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r8.anchor: مثابا عليه مقبولا عنده تعالى بحسن القبول وفسر بعضهم السعي ههنا بالعمل الذي يعبر عنه بفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r9.claim: The root sense of سعي is brisk walking, below running, and it often denotes striving in good deeds; Alusi cites alqama ibn Sad's verse as evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r9.anchor: وأصل السعي كما قال الراغب المشي السريع وهو دون العدو ويستعمل للجد في الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r4.claim: The afterlife seeker represents a clear spiritual disposition and sound nature, and makes the effort suited to it by following the path approved by revealed law.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r4.anchor: لاستقامة وما ترتضيه الشريعة وقال بعضهم : السعي إلى الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r5.claim: Some distinguish bodily striving for worldly aims, striving with the heart for the afterlife, and striving with focused aspiration for God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : السعي إلى الدنيا بالأبدان والسعي إلى الآخرة بالقلوب والسعي إلى الله تعالى بالهمم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r6.claim: True faith remains firm and is not shaken by storms of doubt; the accepted effort is rewarded.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r6.anchor: ( وهو مؤمن ) ثابت الإيمان لا تزعزعه عواصف الشبه ( فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا ) مقبولا مثابا عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r7.speaker: أبو حفص
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r7.claim: Abu Hafs defines appreciated effort as free of ostentation, reputation-seeking, self-regard, and desire for compensation, dedicated solely to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r7.anchor: وعن أبي حفص أن السعي المشكور ما لم يكم مشوبا برياء ولا بسمعة ولا برؤية نفس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r7.claim: Afterlife-seekers must strive as its pursuit requires and be believers; their effort is accepted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r7.anchor: {ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها} عمل عملها، {وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا} مقبولا.

QASHANI:17:18-21/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:18-21/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:18-21/r3.claim: The hereafter-seeker has pure readiness and a sound original nature; when faith and good works fulfill its true conditions, God rewards the effort by granting its object.
QASHANI:17:18-21/r3.anchor: لصفاء استعداده وسلامة فطرته وقام بشرائط إرادته من الإيمان والعمل الصالح

QASHANI:17:18-21/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:18-21/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:18-21/r4.claim: True desire and seeking arise only with readiness; the desired perfection already exists potentially in the decree, and proper effort brings it from unseen potential into visible actuality.
QASHANI:17:18-21/r4.anchor: والإرادة الصادقة لا يكونان إلا عند حصول استعداد المطلوب

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r1.claim: The proper effort for the afterlife means doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden, rather than inventing acts of devotion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r1.anchor: وهو الإتيان بما أمر به، والانتهاء عما نهى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r2.claim: The preposition in “strives for it” signals intention and sincerity.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r3.claim: Faith must be sound, without either associating partners with God or denial; it is the essential condition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r3.anchor: إيمانا صحيحا لا شرك معه ولا تكذيب فإنه العمدة

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r4.claim: Those who meet the three conditions have effort accepted by God and recompensed; God’s thanking obedience means rewarding it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r4.anchor: من الله تعالى أي مقبولا عنده مثابا عليه،

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r6.claim: Seeking the afterlife must be joined to its proper effort: actions pleasing to God as prescribed in the Book and Sunna, not unsupported practices; intention needs action, actually when possible and by capacity when not.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r6.anchor: وهو ما كانت جديرة به من العمل بما يرضي الله بما شرعه في كتابه وسنة رسوله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r7.speaker: بعض السلف
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r7.claim: Some early authorities say work is useless without established faith, sincere intention, and correct action; the author identifies this firmness with the surah's ideal of excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r7.anchor: من لم يكن له ثلاث لم ينفعه عمله : إيمان ثابت , ونية صادقة , وعمل مصيب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r8.claim: The afterlife seeker must be a steadfast believer; only then is the effort accepted and repaid with multiplied reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r9.claim: Worldly wealth may be given to David and Solomon for God's favored work or withheld from another as an honor, never as humiliation; status before God depends on deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r9.anchor: مع أن بعضهم نفتح عليه الأبواب الدنيا كداود وسليمان عليهما الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r10.claim: Whether worldly provision is present or absent, it neither honors nor disgraces its recipient; real status before God comes from deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r10.anchor: فالحاصل أنها إن وجدت عند الوالي لم تشرفهن وإن عدمت عنه لم تحقره

DURR-FULL:v5p254/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r10.claim: God thanks the person for a little good and overlooks much of the person's shortcomings.
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r10.anchor: وفي قوله: {ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا} قال: شكر الله له اليسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.claim: The surrounding passage gradually teaches that people acquire their own deeds by choice and bear their own account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.anchor: تدريجا في التبيان للناس بأن أعمالهم من كسبهم واختيارهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.claim: The afterlife-minded group knows true success lies beyond this life, follows divinely guided works through the messengers, and is rewarded according to its aspiration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.anchor: وقسم علم أن الفوز الحق هو فيما بعد هذه الحياة فعمل للآخرة مقتفيا ما هداه الله إليه من الأعمال بواسطة رسله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.claim: The contrast between the two sentences supplies an added, contextual restriction: the first person wants the immediate world alone.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.claim: The present tense depicts renewed worldly desire, while the past tense and omitted kāna make afterlife desire sound settled and especially worthy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.anchor: والاختلاف بين جملة من كان يريد العاجلة } وجملة { ومن أراد الآخرة } بجعل الفعل مضارعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r2.claim: Saʿy literally means walking rather than running; here it denotes good works that lead to the afterlife as a traveler reaches a destination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r2.anchor: وحقيقة السعي المشي دون العدو ، فسعي الآخرة هو الأعمال الصالحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r3.claim: The possessive construction is a verbal noun related semantically to its object, and saʿy is an absolute object specifying kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r3.anchor: وإضافته إلى ضمير الآخرة من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله في المعنى ، أي السعي لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r4.claim: Wanting the afterlife without striving is self-deception; any aim needs the actions that bring it about.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r4.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه على أن إرادة خير الآخرة من غير سعي غرور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak’s poem rebukes hoping for salvation without following its path, like expecting a ship to sail on dry land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r5.anchor: قال عبد الله بن المبارك : ترجو النجاة ولم تسلك مسالكها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r6.claim: The circumstantial clause is nominal to signal stable, enduring faith; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares this to the wording about persevering believers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r7.claim: The demonstrative points out that people described as seeking the afterlife merit the announced reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r7.anchor: للتنبيه على أن المشار إليهم جديرون بما سيخبر به عنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r8.claim: Calling the effort thanked is a rational metaphor: the worker is approved, and describing the work conveys approval of its doer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r8.anchor: والسعي المشكور هو المشكور ساعيه ، فوصفه به مجاز عقلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p61/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p61/r1.claim: Kāna indicates that the effort was already worthy of thanks in worldly life, while obedience also brings later reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p61/r1.anchor: والتعبير ب { كان } في { كان سعيهم مشكورا } للدلالة على أن الوصف تحقق فيه من قبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r6.claim: Seeking the afterlife requires certain belief in it, in God, and in His messages; these elements are interdependent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r6.anchor: إرادة يقين بها وإيمان وبها وبالله ورسالاته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r7.claim: The required effort is sustained good works and speech according to the law; God rewards and forgives deeds He thanks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r7.anchor: أن يسعى لها سعيها وهو ملازمة أعمال الخير وأقواله على حكم الشرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r8.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r8.claim: A report says God thanked and forgave a man who gave water to a thirsty dog.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r8.anchor: في حديث الرجل الذي سقى الكلب العاطش فشكر الله له فغفر له

SULAMI:v1p385/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p385/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p385/r1.claim: Al-Qasim says seeking the afterlife requires rightly directed effort: it must accord with the law and be grounded in faith, since outwardly upright seekers may lack lasting faith and good efforts may go unaccepted.
SULAMI:v1p385/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : في قوله ﴿ ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها ﴾ بشرط الإرادة بحسن السعاية

SULAMI:v1p385/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p385/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p385/r2.claim: Some distinguish bodily striving in worldly life, striving with hearts toward the afterlife, and striving toward God through spiritual aspiration.
SULAMI:v1p385/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : السعي في الدنيا بالأبدان ، والسعي إلى الآخرة بالقلوب ، والسعي إلى الله تعالى بالهمم

SULAMI:v1p385/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p385/r3.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p385/r3.claim: Abu Hafs says praised striving is free from ostentation, reputation-seeking, self-regard, and desire for reward, being purely for God alone.
SULAMI:v1p385/r3.anchor: قال أبو حفص : السعي المشكور ما لم يكن مشوبا برياء . ولا سمعة ، ولا رؤية نفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#3/r1.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking Paradise and performing the deeds appropriate to it; faith is required for deeds to be valid, and God accepts, rewards, and praises this striving.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#3/r1.anchor: يعني الجنة وسعى لها سعيها أي عمل لها العمل الذي يصلح لها وانما قال وهو مؤمن لأن الايمان شرط في صحة الاعمال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r1.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking its abode and delights by the proper path, namely following the Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r1.anchor: أي: طلب ذلك من طريقه وهو متابعة الرسول {وهو مؤمن}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r2.claim: The seeker must believe in the heart, affirming reward and requital; then the person’s effort is accepted and appreciated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r2.anchor: أي: وقلبه مؤمن، أي: مصدق بالثواب والجزاء {فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا}

JISHUMI:v6p4183/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r1.claim: The passage urges seeking the afterlife: its seeker attains it and may also attain worldly good, whereas a worldly seeker may attain neither.
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r1.anchor: الآخرة وربما لا ينال الدنيا أيضا.

JISHUMI:v6p4183/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r2.claim: The praiseworthy effort that merits Paradise requires faith and good works, against the Murjiʾa.
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن السعي المشكور الموجب للجنة الإيمان والعمل الصالح

JISHUMI:v6p4183/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r3.claim: The disobedience and willing mentioned are human acts, supporting the author's doctrine of created acts.
JISHUMI:v6p4183/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن الفسق فعلهم، وكذلك الإرادة،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r3.claim: The pious believer has chosen the afterlife's riches and is indifferent to worldly allotment; worldly poverty may even help the goal.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r3.anchor: وأما المؤمن التقي فقد اختار مراده وهو غنى الآخرة ، فما يبالي : أوتي حظا من الدنيا أو لم يؤت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r10.claim: The praised effort is the proper effort and its due allotment of righteous deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r10.anchor: حقها من السعي وكفاءها من الأعمال الصالحة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r11.claim: Three conditions make effort rewarded: seeking the afterlife and turning away from delusion, performing commanded acts and avoiding prohibitions, and sound faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r11.anchor: اشترط ثلاث شرائط في كون السعي مشكورا : إرادة الآخرة بأن يعقد بها همه ويتجافى عن دار الغرور ، والسعي فيما كلف من الفعل والترك . والإيمان الصحيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r12.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r12.claim: An early authority says works do not benefit without three things: firm faith, sincere intention, and correct action, and cites this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r12.anchor: وعن بعض المتقدمين : من لم يكن معه ثلاث لم ينفعه عمله : إيمان ثابت ، ونية صادقة ، وعمل مصيب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r13.claim: God's gratitude means His reward for obedience.

MUQATIL:17:19-21/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:19-21/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:19-21/r1.claim: The righteous who seek the Hereafter do its proper work while affirming God's oneness; God thanks their effort by rewarding them with Paradise.
MUQATIL:17:19-21/r1.anchor: من الأبرار بعمله الحسن، وهو مؤمن، يعني بالدار الآخرة

MUQATIL:17:19-21/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:19-21/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:19-21/r2.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Bilal the muezzin and others.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r1.claim: The phrase about striving for the afterlife can mean making it the direct object of striving, or performing the effort it deserves through adequate righteous deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r1.anchor: هو مفعول به أو حقها من السعى وكفاءها من الأعمال الصالحة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r2.claim: Faith means affirming God's promises and threats.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r3.claim: A believer's afterlife-directed effort is accepted by God and rewarded.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r4.speaker: بعض السلف
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r4.claim: Some early authorities say deeds do not benefit without three conditions: firm faith, sincere intention, and sound action; the verse requires afterlife intent, commanded effort, and firm faith.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r4.anchor: عن بعض السلف من لم يكن معه ثلاث لم ينفعه عمله إيمان ثابت ونية صادقة وعمل مصيب

QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r3.claim: Seeking the afterlife means doing its deeds of obedience while believing, since acts are accepted only from a believer; the effort is accepted, not rejected.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r3.anchor: أي عمل لها عملها من الطاعات.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r4.claim: Another explanation of gratitude is that good deeds are multiplied tenfold, seventyfold, seven hundredfold, or many times over.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r4.anchor: وقيل: مضاعفا أي تضاعف لهم الحسنات إلى عشر، وإلى سبعين وإلى سبعمائة ضعف،

QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r5.claim: When asked about a millionfold reward for a good deed, Abu Hurayra says he heard the Prophet promise two millionfold.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة وقد قيل له: أسمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r1.claim: The first condition is intending the afterlife’s reward; without that intention an act does not benefit, as the verse about human striving and the saying about intentions indicate.
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r1.anchor: الشرط الأول : أن يريد بعمله الآخرة أي ثواب الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r2.claim: Intention matters because the purpose of deeds is to illuminate the heart through knowing and loving God, which requires intending worship and obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r2.anchor: المقصود من الأعمال استنارة القلب بمعرفة الله تعالى ومحبته

RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r3.claim: The second condition is pursuing the afterlife by valid acts of worship; idolatrous approaches remain invalid even when their practitioners intend devotion.
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r3.anchor: أن يكون العمل الذي يتوصل به إلى الفوز بثواب الآخرة من الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r4.claim: Some idolaters claim they cannot worship God directly, so they worship stars or angels as devoted intermediaries; Razi rejects this as invalid.
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r4.anchor: يقولون : إله العالم أجل وأعظم من أن يقدر الواحد منا

RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r5.claim: Others say their idols depict prophets and saints and are meant to secure their intercession; Razi also rejects this path.
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r5.anchor: والتأويل الثاني لهم : أنهم قالوا : نحن اتخذنا هذه التماثيل على صور الأنبياء والأولياء

RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r6.claim: He also reports that people in India seek closeness to God by killing or burning themselves, but says this too is an invalid route.
RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r6.anchor: وأيضا نقل عن الهند : أنهم يتقربون إلى الله تعالى بقتل أنفسهم تارة

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r1.claim: Faith is the third condition; without it acts of piety do not earn reward, while meeting all three conditions makes the effort appreciated and accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r1.anchor: وهذا الشرط معتبر ، لأن الشرط في كون أعمال البر موجبة للثواب تقدم الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r2.claim: Gratitude comprises recognizing the recipient as a benefactor, praising them verbally, and acting in ways that honor them; God treats the obedient in all three ways.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r2.anchor: الشكر عبارة عن مجموع أمور ثلاثة : اعتقاد كونه محسنا في تلك الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r3.speaker: جعفر بن حرب
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r3.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Harb argues that faith must be created by God because otherwise thanking God for it would be improper praise for another’s act.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r3.anchor: رأيت في كتب المعتزلة أن جعفر بن حرب حضر عنده واحد من أهل السنة وقال : الدليل على أن الإيمان حصل بخلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r4.speaker: ثمامة بن الأشرس
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r4.claim: Thumama replies that people thank God for the capacity, intellect, revealed books, and proofs He provides, while God thanks them for the faith they perform.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r4.anchor: فدخل ثمامة بن الأشرس وقال : إنما نمدح الله تعالى ونشكره على ما أعطانا من القدرة والعقل

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r5.claim: Razi reconciles the positions: God supplies the complete power and motive, while the servant performs the act of faith, so both God and servant can rightly receive thanks.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r5.anchor: مجموع القدرة مع الداعي يوجب الفعل كلام واضح

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.claim: He classifies actions by whether they aim at worldly good, afterlife good, both together, or neither; the verse directly treats the first two.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.anchor: فإما أن يقصد بذلك الفعل تحصيل خيرات الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.claim: When afterlife motive outweighs worldly motive, Razi presents disagreement: a divine report rejects works involving association, while one analysis denies purity if motives combine and another accepts the dominant afterlife motive.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.anchor: أنا أغنى الأغنياء عن الشرك من عمل عملا أشرك فيه غيري تركته وشريكه

RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.claim: Equal motives or a stronger worldly motive are agreed to make the act unaccepted, though either is better than seeking worldly benefit alone.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.anchor: وأما إذا كان طلب الدنيا وطلب الآخرة متعادلين ، أو كان طلب الدنيا راجحا

RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.claim: On acting without any motive, those who require a motive say it cannot occur; those who do not require one deem it inwardly ineffective and outwardly forbidden as pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.anchor: هذا بناء على أن صدور الفعل من القادر هل يتوقف على حصول الداعي أم لا

STUDYQURAN:17:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r2.claim: God appreciates sincere believers’ efforts for the Hereafter; His appreciation, literally thankfulness, is their reward there.
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r2.anchor: God’s appreciation (lit. “thankfulness”) for their deeds is the reward He grants them in the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:17:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r3.claim: This verse grounds judging deeds by intentions: reward requires intending good, earnestly attempting it, and being a believer, without requiring completion or success.
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r3.anchor: This verse is an important basis for the Islamic doctrine that deeds are judged according to their intentions

STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.claim: Those desiring the ephemeral may include people performing apparently pious acts hypocritically or only for worldly gain.
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.anchor: Those who desire the ephemeral in v. 18 may include not only those whose worldly desires lead them to outwardly sinful behavior

STUDYQURAN:17:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r5.claim: The Prophet’s hadith says deeds are according to intentions, illustrated by emigrants whose reward depends on whether they emigrated for God or worldly benefit such as marriage.
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r5.anchor: the Prophet said in a famous ḥadīth, “Deeds are only according to intentions, and verily each shall have what he intended

TAB-FULL:v14p537/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r1.claim: The afterlife-seeker works the work appropriate to it: obedience that pleases God, while believing in God's reward, unlike the worldly seeker who denies it.
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r1.anchor: للآخرة سعي الآخرة، ومعناه: وعمل لها عملها لمعرفة السامعين بمعنى ذلك

TAB-FULL:v14p537/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r2.claim: In سعى لها سعيها, the feminine pronoun refers to the afterlife; the wording means doing the work of the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r2.anchor: للآخرة سعي الآخرة، ومعناه: وعمل لها عملها لمعرفة السامعين بمعنى ذلك

TAB-FULL:v14p537/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r3.claim: God thanks these believers by rewarding their good works well and forgiving their bad ones through mercy.
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r3.anchor: وشكر الله إياهم على سعيهم ذلك حسن جزائه لهم على أعمالهم الصالحة

TAB-FULL:v14p537/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r4.claim: Qatāda says God rewards their good deeds and overlooks their bad deeds.
TAB-FULL:v14p537/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا} [الإسراء: 19] شكر الله لهم حسناتهم

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.claim: After discussing worldly destruction following a prophetic mission, the passage turns to afterlife punishment, reward, and the general principle governing both.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.anchor: عاد إلى بيان سنته في التعذيب الأخروي والإثابة فيها في هذه الآية والآيتين بعدها

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r3.claim: Saʿy means brisk walking, less than running, and is also used for earnest effort toward good or evil.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r3.anchor: السعي المشي السريع وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر خيرا كان أو شرا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r4.claim: The afterlife sought here means the next life itself, and the earlier argument also rejects narrowing the phrase to intending it through one's deeds.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r4.anchor: أي الحياة الآخرة نظير ما تقدم من قوله { من كان يريد العاجلة }

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r5.claim: The possessive wording makes the effort specific to the afterlife: one must strive in a manner fitting for it, exerting full effort in good deeds grounded in certain reason or legal proof.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r5.anchor: ويستفاد منه أن سعيه لها يجب أن يكون سعيا يليق بها ويحق لها

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r6.claim: Belief means God and entails divine oneness, prophethood, and resurrection; the explicit condition requires sound belief including tawhid and acknowledgment of prophethood.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r6.anchor: فإن من لا يعترف بإحدى الخصال الثلاث لا يعده الله سبحانه في كلامه مؤمنا به

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r7.claim: God thanks the believers' effort by accepting it well and praising its doer; both reward and subsequent praise are grace, with praise being grace upon grace.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r7.anchor: وقوله { فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا } أي يشكره الله بحسن قبوله والثناء على ساعيه

TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.claim: Afterlife-directed deeds reliably reach their ends, unlike worldly causes, since God says the effort is thanked but worldly provision is only what He wills for whom He wills.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.anchor: وفي الآيتين دلالة على أن الأسباب الأخروية وهي الأعمال لا تتخلف عن غاياتها بخلاف الأسباب الدنيوية

TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.claim: A reported taxonomy divides agents into those seeking this world, the afterlife, both, or neither; mixed motives then divide according to which desire predominates or whether they are equal.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.anchor: والتقسيم الحاصر أن كل فاعل إما أن يريد بفعله العاجلة فقط أو يريد الآخرة فقط أو يريدهما معا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.claim: The reported discussion says scholars disagree over accepting mixed-motive deeds when afterlife intent predominates, but agree against deeds where worldly motive predominates or ties.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.anchor: ونقل اختلاف العلماء في قبول هذا النوع من العمل، ونقل اتفاقهم على عدم قبول ما يترجح فيه باعث الدنيا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.claim: The fourth type is impossible for those who require every voluntary act to have a motive; others say such an act has no inner effect but remains outwardly forbidden.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.anchor: وأما القسم الرابع عند القائلين بأن صدور الفعل من القادر يتوقف على حصول الداعي فهو ممتنع الحصول

TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.claim: These verses classify a person's ultimate life-goal, not the acceptance of every individual act: seeking this world treats it as the end, while seeking the afterlife treats this world as a stage toward it.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.anchor: أن الآيات الكريمة ليست في مقام بيان حكم الرد والقبول بالنسبة إلى كل عمل صدر عن عامل

TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r3.claim: Afterlife-seekers can still fail to strive properly or lack belief, but the verse selects the believing person whose effort fits the afterlife because it identifies the roots of happiness and misery.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r3.anchor: ولم يذكر في كلامه تعالى إلا حكم طائفة خاصة وهي من أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن

TABRISI:17:19-22/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:19-22/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:19-22/r2.claim: Seeking the hereafter requires obedience, avoiding sins, and belief in God's unity and messengers; the effort is accepted.
TABRISI:17:19-22/r2.anchor: أي فعل الطاعات وتجنب المعاصي وهو مع ذلك مصدق بتوحيد الله مقر بأنبيائه

TABRISI:17:19-22/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:19-22/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:17:19-22/r3.claim: He says God's gratitude consists in multiplying good deeds and overlooking sins.
TABRISI:17:19-22/r3.anchor: عن قتادة والمعنى أنا أحللنا سعيهم محل ما يشكر عليه في حسن الجزاء

TABRISI:17:19-22/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:19-22/r4.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:17:19-22/r4.claim: He urges pursuit of the hereafter: its seeker attains it and may also gain the world, while a worldly seeker may fail at both.
TABRISI:17:19-22/r4.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال: اطلبوا الآخرة فما رأيت طالبا لها إلا نالها

THALABI:v6p91/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p91/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p91/r8.claim: The afterlife seeker must strive properly and be a believer; such striving is accepted rather than rejected.
THALABI:v6p91/r8.anchor: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وعمل لها عملها وهو مؤمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās understands the Hereafter as Paradise; the commentators also relate the phrase to seeking the reward or good of the Hereafter, as in 3:145.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r2.claim: Striving for the Hereafter means carrying out God's obligations and fulfilling His rights.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد العمل بفرائض الله والقيام بحقوقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r3.claim: The striving is accepted only with faith, since God accepts no good deed except from a believer; gratitude means multiplying good deeds, erasing sins, and raising ranks.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r3.anchor: فإن الله لا يقبل حسنة إلا من مصدق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r3.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking Paradise and fulfilling God's obligations; faith is necessary because God accepts good only from believers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r3.anchor: { ومن أراد الآخرة } الجنة { وسعى لها سعيها } عمل بفرائض الله { وهو مؤمن } لأن الله سبحانه لا يقبل حسنة إلا من مؤمن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r4.claim: The believers' accepted efforts are appreciated by multiplying their good deeds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r4.anchor: { فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا } تضاعف لهم الحسنات.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r5.claim: Striving for the Hereafter means doing the deeds appropriate to it, with sincere faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r5.anchor: قوله: {ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها} [الإسراء: 19] عمل لها عملها. {وهو مؤمن} [الإسراء: 19] مخلص بالإيمان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet saying God does not accept a servant’s deed until He is pleased with the servant’s utterance.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r6.anchor: خالد، عن الحسن، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا يقبل الله عمل عبد حتى يرضى قوله» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r7.claim: The promised accepted striving means the person’s deeds, which God thanks and rewards with Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r7.anchor: قال: {فأولئك كان سعيهم} [الإسراء: 19] يعني: عملهم. {مشكورا} [الإسراء: 19] ، يعني: يشكر الله أعمالهم حتى يثيبهم الله به الجنة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says the thankful reward means God repays them for their deeds.

SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r1.claim: سعيها has two parses: direct object meaning the deeds appropriate to the Hereafter, or a cognate accusative with لها meaning for its sake.
SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { سعيها }: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه مفعول به لأن المعنى: وعمل لها عملها.

SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r2.claim: وهو مؤمن is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of سعى.
SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r2.anchor: قوله { وهو مؤمن } هذه الجملة حال من فاعل " سعى ".

ELMALILI:17:19-22/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:19-22/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:19-22/r1.claim: The afterlife-seeker must pursue it with fitting effort while believing; such people’s striving is appreciated.
ELMALILI:17:19-22/r1.anchor: ona iman ederek lâyıkı vechile sa‘y de eylerse

ELMALILI:17:19-22/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:19-22/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:19-22/r6.claim: Every effort needs power; the greatest power is truth and truth begins with monotheism, making faith the first condition for afterlife-worthy striving and explaining why the commands begin with tawhid.
ELMALILI:17:19-22/r6.anchor: En büyük kuvvet ise haktır. Hakkın başı da tevhiddir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.claim: Worldly advantages are not true superiority; seeking the hereafter concerns one's aim, not merely the type of work, since worldly tasks can serve the hereafter and worship can serve worldly gain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.anchor: burada yapılan iş değil, o işle neyin hedeflendiğinin altı çizilmekte, yani niyetlere dikkat çekilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3.claim: The Prophet teaches that deeds are judged according to intentions.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r4.claim: A person seeks the hereafter by doing even worldly work honestly under God's rules, remembering accountability, and hoping for God's reward; each receives according to intention.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r4.anchor: dünya işi yaparken de bunu Allah’ın hükümlerine uyarak, âhirette Allah’a hesap vereceğini düşünerek, sevabını Allah’tan umarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r5.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r5.claim: A good deed requires seeking afterlife reward, performing the actions that earn it, and doing so with faith; faith makes the other conditions meaningful and effective.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r5.anchor: Zemahşerî, II, 356). Âyette inanmanın şart olarak yer alması, diğerlerinin anlamlı hale gelmesi

ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r1.claim: Here 'believer' entails recognizing God's absolute oneness and willingly accepting guidance through prophetic revelation, since striving for the hereafter presupposes belief and accountability.
ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r1.anchor: the term "believer" relates, in this context, to a cognition of God's absolute oneness and uniqueness

ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r2.claim: Although the Arabic sentence is singular before the final clause, Asad renders the pronouns in the plural to match that clause and normal Arabic usage.
ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r2.anchor: in view of the next clause, which is expressed in the plural, it is preferable to render these pronouns

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r3.claim: Seeking the afterlife means preferring it, intending it, and pursuing the deeds prescribed for salvation; faith is the indispensable condition without which intention and effort do not save.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r3.anchor: ومن أراد الآخرة أي ثواب الآخرة بأن يؤثرها على الدنيا، ويعقد إرادته بها وسعى فيما كلف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r4.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r4.claim: An early authority says work is useless without firm faith, sincere intention, and sound action, and cites this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r4.anchor: وعن بعض المتقدمين من لم يكن معه ثلاث لم ينفعه عمله: إيمان ثابت، ونية صادقة، وعمل مصيب، وتلا هذه الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r5.claim: The plural أولئك refers to people described by the singular relative من because its meaning is collective; God rewards and praises their obedience, while He alone truly deserves gratitude.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r5.anchor: فأولئك إشارة إلى من اتصف بهذه الأوصاف وراعى معنى من فلذلك كان بلفظ الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r6.claim: God’s thanking a servant means praising and rewarding the obedient person; the human response is praise for reason, revelation, books, and proofs granted by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r6.anchor: ومعنى شكره تعالى المطيع الإثناء عليه وثوابه على طاعته

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r1.claim: The names of the vowel marks derive from articulation: ḍamma closes and raises the lips, fatḥa opens the mouth, and kasra lowers the jaw; jazm means cutting, while the senses of waqf and sukūn are evident.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r1.anchor: وأما الجزم فهو القطع وأما أنه لم سمي وقفا وسكونا فعلته ظاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r2.claim: Some grammarians reserve fatḥa, ḍamma, kasra, and waqf for built forms, while the other four terms name inflectional states.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r2.anchor: منهم من زعم أن الفتح والضم والكسر والوقف أسماء للأحوال البنائية

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r3.claim: Others use the first four names for both built and inflected states, treating the second four as narrower names for inflection; the first set is thus genus to the second.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r3.anchor: وجعل الأربعة الثانية أسماء للأحوال الإعرابية فتكون الأربعة الأولى بالنسبة إلى الأربعة الثانية كالجنس

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh calls the vocalic states al-majārī and counts eight.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r4.anchor: أن سيبويه يسميها بالمجاري ويقول : هي ثمانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī explains the name al-majārī by saying the so-called movement is a voiced sound produced as breath flows and extends after a consonant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r5.anchor: فهذا الحرف المصوت إنما حدث لجريان نفسه وامتداده

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r6.speaker: المازني
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r6.claim: Al-Māzinī says Sībawayh errs by calling the states of built words al-majārī, since only changing inflectional states should count as things that flow.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r6.anchor: قال المازني : غلط سيبويه في تسميته الحركات البنائية بالمجاري

RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that built forms change between connected speech and pause, so their states are not wholly fixed and can still be called al-majārī.
RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r7.anchor: المبنيات قد تحرك عند الدرج ولا تحرك عند الوقف فلم تكن تلك الأحوال لازمة لها مطلقا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.claim: The third sense is deeds or striving: the source applies it both to striving for the afterlife and to people's divergent efforts.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أنه في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : -

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r6.claim: Saʿy can mean work or action: seeking the afterlife with its saʿy means doing the work it requires.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.claim: In conditional clauses, he uses the present for actions expected to recur and the past for actions that do not or should not recur; examples include repeated gratitude versus one-time disbelief and accidental versus deliberate killing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.anchor: استعمال فعل المضارع مع الشرط يكون إذا كان مضمون أن يتكرر.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p95/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p95/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p95/r2.claim: The past marks desire for the one afterlife as a single act; present tense marks recurrent desires for reward, which arise with each deed.
